RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday,  the August 31, 2007/Bhadrapada 9, 1929 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs,
Food and Public Distribution; Health and Family Welfare;
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions — 20
82
High speed trains
*261. DR. K. KESHAVA RAO: Will
the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that his Ministry
is considering to introduce high speed trains
which would run at the speed of 350
kilometre per hour across the country;
(b) if so, the details of the routes and
names of the States which have expressed
interest in the high speed lines;
(c) whether any request has been
received from the Government of Andhra
Pradesh in this regard;
(d) if so, the response of his Ministry;
and
(e) by when the proposal would be
taken up?
Failure of PDS
*262. DR. GY AN PRAKASH
PILANIA: Will the Minister of
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to
state:
(a) the quantum of wheat, rice, sugar,
kerosene, etc. fixed per person per BPL/
APL card, through PDS;
(b) whether it is sufficient;
(c) the details of malpractices in PDS;
(d) the cases detected/registered and
their disposal, during the last three years;
(e) how many ration dealers were
sentenced with imprisonment for
misappropriation/selling/diverting the items
in open market, during the last three years,
year-wise;
(f) the measures taken by Government
to check the malpractices;
(g) Government's nine point action plan
for tackling diversion of PDS items and its
implementation; and
(h) whether PDS has failed in the
country?
Sanction of new rail line projects in
Rajasthan
*263. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether his Ministry has not

83
accepted the proposal of some new rail
line projects because of paucity of funds;
and
(b) in view of the poor railway network
in Rajasthan, whether Government are
going to accept the projects i.e., to link
Bhiwadi to Delhi-Ahmedabad broad gauge
railway line, Jaisalmer to Sanu, Jaisalmer
to Barmer, and Jaipur to Nathdwara for
industrial, mining and tourism development
of the State?
Wasteful expenditure due to lack of
comprehensive planning
*264. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Comptroller and Auditor
General has pulled up Railways for lack of
comprehensive planning which resulted in
wasteful expenditure on track renewal
works on sections identified for gauge
conversion and the improvement in track
parameters is not commensurate with large
number of track renewal works undertaken
by Railways;
(b) whether CAG noted that the
budgetary control mechanism was
inadequate as seen from the savings over
some zonal railways and excess expenditure
over other during the same financial year
for the last five years both under divisional
and special railway safety fund; and
(c) what action his Ministry has taken
on the CAG's report?
Non-payment of arrears by sugar
mills in Uttar Pradesh
†*265. SHRI SATYAVRAT
CHATURVEDI:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the sugar
mills in Uttar Pradesh under public sector,
cooperative sector and private sector owe
an amount of rupees 13445.41 lakhs,
9313.77 lakhs and 26413.78 lakhs
respectively for the price of sugarcane for
the season 2006-07;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
sugar mills under private sector in Uttar
Pradesh owe an amount of rupees 8455.02
lakhs for the price of sugarcane for the
2004-05 season and the seasons prior
thereto;
(c) if so, the steps taken by Government
to expedite the payment to farmers; and
(d) by when the farmers would get the
full payment?
Banned drugs in circulation
*266. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
SHRI VINAY KATIYAR:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether a number of drugs which
are banned globally, are being sold in the
country;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(c) whether some drugs which are
banned in the country, are still available in
the market; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken in this regard?

SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY:

pleased to state:

for reservation out of the total number of
berths under Tatkal Reservation System;
(b) whether the number of general
reservation berths has not been reduced
following implementation of Tatkal
Reservation System;
(c) if so, whether reduction in number
of general reservation berths has not
compounded the problems of passengers;
and

Farmers’ indebtedness
1984. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether indebtedness of farmers is
increasing day by day and in some States it
has reached up to 60 per cent;
(b) if so, what are the figures of farmers’
indebtedness, State-wise;
(c) whether Government would provide
package to indebted farmers throughout the
country particularly to the farmers of Uttar
Pradesh who are waiting for their dues to
be cleared by the sugar factories; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Supply of milk products at DMS
depots
†1985. SHRI VINAY KATIYAR: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the supply of products such
as pure ghee, butter-100 gm, curd and sweet
milk apart from milk has been discontinued
in the depots of Delhi Milk Scheme;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether there is any scheme for
restarting the sale of the said items; and
(d) if so, by when it would be done?
Number of DMS employees
†1986. SHRI VINAY KATIYAR: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any plan to reduce
the number of employees of the Delhi Milk
Scheme; and
(b) if so, by when it will be done?
Loss of livestock due to mechanised
slaughter of animals
†1987. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
DR. NARAYAN SINGH
MANAKLAO:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are worried
about the fact that thousands of healthy
animals mostly Bovine, are taken to the

460
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
mechanised slaughter houses of
metropolitan cities and other countries
from many States where their killing is
banned;
(b) if so, what steps have been taken to
stop/to get stopped this continuous loss
of livestock;
(c) whether any project is being run by
the Central Government itself for the
protection and utilization of animals;
(d) if not, whether any assistance is
being provided to the projects running in
the States; and
(e) whether there is any provision to
provide assistance to States; if so, the
details thereof for the last three years?
Farm subsidies
1988. DR.  K. KESHAVA RAO: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that developed
countries like the US and Japan are giving
30 per cent of their GDP towards farm
subsidies;
(b) whether it is a fact that a country
like India where about 63 per cent depend
on agriculture is extending a scarce share of
the GDP towards subsidies; and
(c) if so, what steps Government would
take to step up farm subsidies to reduce
interest rates for agriculture and self-help
groups?
Subsidy for Vidarbha cotton growers
†1989. SHRI SANJAY RAUT:
SHRI DATTA MEGHE:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
Members of Parliament from Vidarbha in
Maharashtra have submitted a
memorandum in which they have
demanded subsidy for cotton growers and
to increase the purchase price for their crop;
(b) if so, the action taken in this regard;
and
(c) the arrangements made by
Government to povide subsidy to the
cotton growers in the event of crisis and to
increase the purchase price for their crop
in future?
Corporate farming
1990. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are lots
of shortcomings while promoting corporate
farming in the country;
(b) if so, Government's response
thereto;
(c) whether Government are taking any
initiatives for making long term transparent
policies for making corporate farming
successful in the country; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the
details of steps taken or proposed to set
up strong systems to monitor contracts
and corporate farming so as to avoid
exploitation of the workers/growers and
farmers in the country?
Combating hunger through
investment in agriculture
1991. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Director-General of

461
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
FAO of the UN has recently commented
while in India that India needs to strengthen
its efforts to combat hunger through more
investments in agriculture;
(b) whether India has succeeded to
reduce its share of hungry people from 39
per cent to 20 per cent;
(c) whether according to FAO statistics
for the year 2006, one in four persons
remained hungry in India as compared to
one in five in China; and
(d) what are the steps being taken to
increase investments in agricultural sector?
Declining fertility of soil
